newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG UNDER PRESSURE AHEAD OF MARSEILLE CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG UNDER PRESSURE AHEAD OF MARSEILLE CLASH.

text.p: Paris St Germain, under serious threat from in-form Monaco, must beat arch-rivals Marseille at the Parc des Princes on Friday to remain firmly in command of the French championship.
Monaco, who trail PSG by just three points, host lowly Nancy on Saturday and look likely to win.
It is why the Parisians, still in shock after slumping to a 5-3 defeat in Bordeaux last week, badly need a victory too. But the task is by no means easy.
For Marseille, struggling to recover their past brilliance after two seasons in the second division, this is the match of the season.
"We have been talking about this for weeks. A draw would be a real feat," Marseille defender Hamada Jambay said.
But Gerard Gili, coach of the former European champions, has played down the importance of the clash.
"We're not playing in the same league. PSG are title contenders, we are not," he said.
Fans may have different views and, given the traditional rivalry bewteen the two cities and their clubs, the same security measures have been taken by the police as for an international.

PSG have also been preparing for the match as if it were a European date. "We have worked as hard as before the second leg of our Cup Winners' Cup match against Galatasaray," said president Michel Denisot.
Marseille striker Xavier Gravelaine, transferred from PSG at the beginning of the season, knows exactly what to expect. "They're going to be at their best which may suit us fine," he said.
Both sides face injury problems. Former Marseille defender Benoit Cauet has been declared unfit and will be replaced by young Portuguese international Daniel Kenedy.
Marseille, who have had to cope with an embarrassing number of red cards this season, will be without suspended Ivan Franceschini and Olivier Echouafni.
Experienced captain Jean-Philippe Durand, the only player left from 1993 European Cup victory, is also doubtful.
"We've had to cope with that sort of situation since the start of the season. And this match is not the highlight match of the league season it used to be," said Gili.
"Actually, it is nothing more than another league match which might help us confirm we're back on the right track."
Marseille have not lost in their last three outings.
